Steps.Title: Resolve UI screenshot applicability
Steps.Subtitle: UI routes or no-UI evidence
Steps.Notes: Classify UI applicability from the architecture handoff, project structure, and current-run evidence. Prefer a recorded Run app node. When it is absent, use the runtime-forwarded typed bootstrap decision or a grounded product inspection to identify the declared runnable project file; aliases are optional convenience values, not topology inference. Record a launch-required manifest when a UI target has no live URL. Resolve the deterministic process-run writeback target from TargetProcessRunNodeId, ParentProcessRunNodeId, ProcessRunNodeId, then CurrentProcessRunNodeId. A missing Screenshots child is normal create-or-reuse work owned by store-ui-screenshots, not unavailable writeback or capture work. Record explicit no-UI evidence only when the declared target has no browser-visible surface.

InstructionFragments.Title: Pre-QA screenshot applicability context
InstructionFragments.Content: This screenshot subprocess may run before QA validation. Do not require upstream QA evidence to resolve applicability; use architecture, implementation, acceptance-plan, project-structure, and grounded product context. Runtime command nodes are optional when the child can directly launch the grounded app project.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Architecture handoff, implementation and acceptance-plan context, optional runtime command nodes, route nodes, process run node context, and optional verified upstream runtime/browser evidence when available.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshot applicability manifest with UI routes or explicit no-UI evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: App type, UI/no-UI decision, route list, viewport set, runtime command references or degraded runtime evidence, missing-reference warnings, and the deterministic process-run writeback target with the Screenshots child marked existing or create-required.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may block when UI applicability or route targets are ambiguous.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when UI applicability is contradictory, route targets are empty for a UI app, no concrete launch/browser evidence exists for a UI app, or no-UI evidence is missing for a non-UI target. Missing command nodes or process-run node access are warnings when concrete QA/runtime evidence is available.

Steps.Title: Capture UI screenshots when required
Steps.Subtitle: Current-run browser proof
Steps.Notes: For a UI target, prefer the recorded Run app node. Otherwise read runtime-forwarded typed bootstrap context for the declared runnable project file, use an agreeing launch alias when available, and use grounded product inspection only as a last resort. Do not construct a conventional solution, project, or directory path. workspace_dotnet_run requires a declared runnable project file, never a solution or directory. Capture current-run browser navigation, snapshot, screenshot, console, and cleanup receipts. Begin DOM assertions from the same-run browser snapshot and record selector or locator provenance from that snapshot, a same-run DOM enumeration, or an exact product source read. A zero match from an ungrounded selector is inconclusive, not evidence of absence. Reconcile evaluated state with the same-run snapshot and screenshot; omit an unsupported structured claim or recapture it with an observed locator when they conflict. browser_evaluate is optional and does not replace required snapshot or screenshot receipts. A visible defect that remains grounded after reconciliation is evidence for QA and must continue to assessment, not become a capture retry or a no-UI claim. Capture does not own project-structure writeback: a create-required Screenshots child is normal work for store-ui-screenshots and must not be reported as missing current-run evidence, a fallback, limitation, warning, blocker, or capture next action. Return Completed with ui-capture-complete when capture and cleanup receipts are complete. Return Blocked only when a concrete launch, browser, route, access, policy, or provider boundary prevents grounded evidence.

Zero matches from ungrounded selectors are inconclusive and must be omitted or recaptured with an observed locator.

Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not substitute stale screenshots, chat-only claims, or screenshots from another process run.

Steps.Title: Store screenshots under process run node
Steps.Subtitle: Screenshots project-structure parent
Steps.Notes: Create or reuse a Screenshots parent node under the current process run node. Resolve the writeback parent from TargetProcessRunNodeId, ParentProcessRunNodeId, ProcessRunNodeId, then CurrentProcessRunNodeId, and use a focused project_structure_read with that node id or subtree root. Do not fall back to ProjectNodeId or project root when a process-run target is present. For UI targets, inspect each screenshot, distinguish accepted visual proof from a grounded visual discrepancy, and create image asset nodes under Screenshots for accepted screenshots and diagnostic rejected screenshots. workspace_inspect_image and workspace_analyze_image are required runtime tool receipts only for ui-evidence-stored; call both for every accepted or rejected screenshot and ground the visual reason in the provider-backed result instead of dimensions, filenames, or chat-only descriptions. When source visual target ImageAsset nodes exist, resolve them with project_structure_read, project_structure_asset_get, or project_structure_asset_content_get, then call workspace_analyze_images with the ordered source-target and delivered screenshot paths. If target content is inaccessible, return Blocked with the node id, media path, and failed receipt. Include a Visual target comparison naming the source asset, delivered screenshot, method, and disposition. For UI screenshots, project_structure_node_create and project_structure_asset_create are required runtime tool receipts only for ui-evidence-stored: create or reuse Screenshots with objectType ProjectBlock, objectSubtype delivery, and parentNodeKey set to the process-run node; create one ImageAsset with objectSubtype screenshot per image using its exact sourceWorkspacePath plus explicit sourceFileName and sourceContentType. Label visual discrepancies as diagnostic rejected evidence. Do not infer these tools are unavailable from memory or prompt text. Do not read binary images as text or base64 when sourceWorkspacePath is available; after an invalid base64 upload, retry once with sourceWorkspacePath. Do not write Status: Completed until node creation or reuse and every asset creation succeeds. There is no successful managed-only storage outcome for a UI target. If a write tool is unavailable, denied, or fails, retain a diagnostic failure receipt and return Blocked instead of completing. A visual discrepancy is not a storage blocker: preserve its diagnostic asset for assessment. For an explicitly no-UI target, carry forward the no-UI receipt as managed evidence, select no-ui-evidence-recorded, and do not manufacture images or browser receipts. A missing tool is not no-UI evidence. Do not mutate product files.

InstructionFragments.Title: Development UI screenshot image analysis
InstructionFragments.Content: Use generic workspace image tools only as software-delivery visual evidence for this step: inspect screenshot readability, route correctness, blank/error states, visible UI behavior, and ordered source-target comparisons against project visual target ImageAssets. Do not treat this as generic image interpretation.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Screenshot storage must inspect image files before accepting or rejecting them.
Screenshot storage must ground visual decisions in provider-backed image analysis.
Screenshot storage must compare delivered screenshots with source visual targets when target images exist.
Accepted UI screenshots must be stored under a Screenshots parent node when project-structure writeback is available.
Accepted UI screenshots must be written as ImageAsset nodes when project-structure writeback is available.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot files, browser evidence, and screenshot target manifest.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshots parent node under the process run node and image asset storage receipts that distinguish accepted proof from diagnostic rejected evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Screenshots parent node id from project_structure_node_create and one image asset id from project_structure_asset_create per UI screenshot, with accepted or diagnostic rejected disposition, plus workspace_inspect_image, workspace_analyze_image, and when source visual targets exist workspace_analyze_images receipt refs, Visual target comparison details, rejected images, and no-UI receipt when applicable. Failed UI writeback is a blocked diagnostic, not a completed storage alternative.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Storage reviewer can preserve unusable screenshots as diagnostic evidence; the later evidence-assessment step owns the explicit disposition that QA consumes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: block when required Screenshots storage receipts are missing, invalid, or not materialized before branch routing, or when a capture, image-analysis, project-structure, access, policy, or provider failure prevents durable evidence. Do not block merely because a screenshot shows a grounded visual discrepancy; preserve the rejected evidence and let the assessment step emit the observed-defect disposition. If project-structure writeback tools are available, do not complete until project_structure_node_create and project_structure_asset_create are attempted and successful for each UI screenshot. If project_structure_asset_create or project_structure_node_create is unavailable or denied, return Blocked with the missing tool or operation allowance instead of completing silently.

Steps.Title: Assess UI screenshot evidence disposition
Steps.Subtitle: Accepted proof or observed visual defect
Steps.Notes: Read the screenshot target manifest, stored screenshot receipts, current-run browser and image-analysis evidence when the target has a UI, and any source visual target comparison. For UI evidence, perform the image inspection and analysis for this current execution before selecting the disposition; upstream descriptions and asset ids alone are not proof. Select visual-accepted when UI screenshots satisfy the declared route and visual target. Select visual-defect-observed, not Blocked, when captured current-run evidence demonstrates a blank, error, wrong-route, scaffold, unstyled, non-interactive, or source-target-mismatched UI. Select no-ui-evidence-recorded only when the applicability manifest explicitly classifies the target as having no browser-visible UI and cites its evidence; do not demand browser, image-analysis, or image-asset receipts for that disposition. A missing browser, image tool, or storage tool for a UI target is not no-UI evidence. The completed disposition must name the applicable evidence so parent QA can independently validate and choose its normal quality branch. Return Blocked only when a capture, image-analysis, access, policy, or provider failure prevents the applicable grounded disposition; a product discrepancy by itself is not an execution blocker. This step does not change the product and does not direct a product fix.

InstructionFragments.Title: Development UI screenshot disposition
InstructionFragments.Content: Use current-execution image inspection and analysis to distinguish accepted visual proof from an observed visual defect when the target has a UI. For an explicit no-UI target, record no-ui-evidence-recorded only from the applicability evidence, without inventing browser or image-analysis evidence. A missing UI tool does not prove no UI. A visual defect is evidence for QA, not a reason to report this evidence-assessment step as blocked.

RequiredReceipts.Reason: Screenshot evidence assessment must inspect every dispositioned UI screenshot.
Screenshot evidence assessment must use provider-backed analysis for visual disposition.
Screenshot evidence assessment must compare accessible source visual targets with delivered screenshots.

Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot target manifest and durable screenshot storage receipts, including current-run browser and image-analysis evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: A recorded disposition that is accepted UI proof, an observed visual defect, or explicit no-UI evidence for parent QA.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Exact screenshot and route refs, accepted or diagnostic asset ids, current-run image inspection and analysis receipts and source-target comparison for UI evidence, or explicit no-UI evidence when browser capture is inapplicable, plus the chosen disposition rationale.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The screenshot review specialist records the evidence disposition; the screenshot manager reviews that the parent can act on it without treating product evidence as an infrastructure blocker.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when the applicable durable evidence cannot be produced or read because of a concrete tool, access, policy, or provider failure. Complete with visual-defect-observed when UI evidence itself shows a product defect, and with no-ui-evidence-recorded when browser capture is inapplicable.

Steps.Title: Hand off screenshot writeback evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready visual proof
Steps.Notes: Summarize screenshot applicability, captured routes, Screenshots parent node id, accepted and diagnostic image asset node ids, no-UI evidence, and concrete tool or access blockers for parent QA. Copy the exact evidence-assessment Branch outcome key: visual-accepted, visual-defect-observed, or no-ui-evidence-recorded. visual-defect-observed and no-ui-evidence-recorded are completed evidence handoffs for QA, not child no-go outcomes and not instructions to alter the product. no-ui-evidence-recorded must cite the explicit applicability classification and does not replace non-browser QA. This step writes managed process artifacts only.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot storage receipts, target manifest, and the explicit visual evidence disposition.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Parent-ready screenshot writeback handoff carrying the exact UI or no-UI evidence disposition.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Applicability, node ids, accepted and diagnostic asset ids for UI evidence, route evidence, image-analysis receipts when applicable, no-UI status, exact disposition, and concrete execution blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may hand off visual-accepted, visual-defect-observed, or no-ui-evidence-recorded when it is durably grounded; only genuine evidence-production failures remain blocked.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close with missing Screenshots storage or evidence-disposition records for UI targets. Do not convert a grounded visual-defect-observed or no-ui-evidence-recorded disposition into a blocked child outcome.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Delivery manager owns parent-ready screenshot handoff.

A visual-defect-observed handoff must name the observed discrepancy and its evidence without claiming acceptance. A no-ui-evidence-recorded handoff must cite explicit no-UI rationale without inventing browser or image-analysis proof.
